title: Sliding Window Maximum
summary: For every contiguous length-k window, return its maximum.

contractDetails.constraints: The array has 1–100,000 integers in [−10,000, 10,000]. The window size k is between 1 and the array length.

statement: For every contiguous length-k window, return its maximum. List the maxima in order of increasing window start, beginning at index zero.

examples.explanation: The three windows have maxima 6, 5 and 5.
One copy of 2 leaves, but the other remains in the second window.
There is one window covering the entire input.

constraints: The array has 1–100,000 integers in [−10,000, 10,000]. The window size k is between 1 and the array length.
hints: Conceptual: An earlier smaller value cannot win while a later larger value is still inside the window.
Directional: Keep indices in a deque with their values ordered from largest to smallest.
Implementation: Remove expired indices at the front and dominated indices at the back before appending the new index. Read the front once the window is full.
complexityAnalysis: O(n) time and O(k) auxiliary space excluding output. Each index enters and leaves the deque at most once.
